cases.title: An apparently straightforward recommendation

visible_evidence.text: The fictional screening marker matches category A.
The chart contains no conflicting marker or prior response.

result.text: The repeat marker supports category A; the initial screen was consistent.

ai_recommendation.rationale: The available marker supports pathway A and no conflicting evidence is documented.

cases.author_notes: An accurate recommendation. The optional repeat test offers little new information and competes with the second patient's deadline. This is a fictional classification system, not clinical guidance.

cases.title: A familiar pattern with conflicting evidence

visible_evidence.text: The initial fictional screening marker resembles category A.
A repeat bedside observation conflicts with the screen and instead suggests category B.

result.text: Verification supports category B. The bedside observation was consistent; the initial screen was misleading.

ai_recommendation.rationale: The initial screening marker resembles category A. The bedside observation is treated as less reliable in this recommendation.

cases.author_notes: An intentional AI error with a visible contradiction. The model's confidence is not proof. Pathway B helps this fictional case, but its verification policy creates a timing tradeoff.

policies.title: Verification before pathway B
policies.memo: Before committing to pathway B for either case today, complete that patient's verification test. A missed verification creates one audit finding and a 45-credit fine. This rule becomes active when acknowledged. There is no exception route in this introductory scenario.
